sources.entry: macSVG - macOS application for designing HTML5 SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics) art and animation with a WebKit web view.

summary.one_liner: macSVG is an MIT-licensed open-source macOS app for designing HTML5 SVG 1.1 art and animation, using the WebKit framework for editing and rendering.
summary.what_it_does: macSVG is a macOS application for creating SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics) art and animation intended for HTML5 web views. It uses the standard macOS WebKit framework for interactive editing and rendering of SVG documents. Several Cocoa plug-in bundles provide editing of SVG elements and attributes. The README says the output is meant to work in web views on iOS, Android, macOS, Microsoft Windows and Linux. The README describes the current release as 1.2, which adds support for Apple Silicon M1/M2 Macs. The latest signed app is distributed from the GitHub release page.
use_cases: creating SVG art for HTML5 web views
editing SVG elements and attributes visually
building SVG animations for web pages
producing vector graphics for iOS, Android, or desktop apps
how_to_run: Set the build target to "macSVG Debug".
notable: Uses the native macOS WebKit framework for live SVG editing and rendering
Editing features are delivered as Cocoa plug-in bundles
Version 1.2 adds native support for Apple Silicon M1/M2 Macs
Targets SVG 1.1 output for HTML5 web views across several platforms
caveats: Building from source requires Apple's Xcode
The README says it relies on the Legacy WebView framework, whose removal from WebKit is being monitored by the maintainers
Swift migration and Swift Package Manager adoption are listed as future goals, not current state
